pr_body:
Introduce DB based keyspace notifications (solves #3782)

Some commands can cause a "DB level" event which effects the keyspace.
Commands like swapdb and flushdb will not be reported by the current
keyspace-notifications  mechanism since they do not operate on a key
level.
This PR introduce a new type of notification: "DBEVENT".
the DBEVENT will be reported into a new pubsub channel following a
similar logic as regular keyspace-notifications do.
the reported notification will have the following structure:
__dbevent@0\_\_:<event> <msg>
where the event will match the action (currently swapdb and flushdb)
and the massage will be different for each event (for example sync/async
for flush and the swapped db id in case of swapdb)

this PR contains:
1. add config values to notify-keyspace-events:
  - 'D' (NOTIFY_DBEVENT) - to enable getting DB level notifications
  - 'f' (NOTIFY_FLUSHDB) - to enable flushdb notifications
  - 'w' (NOTIFY_SWAPDB)  - to enable swapdb notifications

2. added notify API notifyDBEvent which is much like notifyKeyspaceEvent
 only instead of key it will accept a generic msg.

3. emit flushdb notification in signalFlushedDb

4. emit swapdb notifications in swapdbCommand

5. added tests in pubsub.tcl for swapdb, flushall, flushdb

Open issues:
- [ ] do we want to issue separate event for each DB on flushall?
- [ ] currently modules will not be notified for db events, since they will
 not get a key. do we want a new module API to handle DB events?
- [ ] do we want 2 separate events for before/after flushdb and swapdb?
pr_comments:
only skimmed though this (the top comment), just dumping my raw thoughts:
considering the low frequency, i don't think we need separate channels for the different variations, we only need for the user to be able to distinguish between them.
i think it's sufficient that FLUSHALL fire one event, and users will know to expect it.
i don't think there's a need for before and after (unlike modules that can get triggers to operations that happen in between).
i don't think there's a need for any of that for modules, since they already have a way to get these events.

> only skimmed though this (the top comment), just dumping my raw thoughts: considering the low frequency

Thank you!

>  i don't think we need separate channels for the different variations, we only need for the user to be able to distinguish between them. 

I think that this mainly aims to provide applications to be able to setup logical separation based on event type. there is no complexity issue here, and it might make it simpler for application code to handle.

>i think it's sufficient that FLUSHALL fire one event, and users will know to expect it. 

I think that the reason is for applications to be able to manage logical separation. If application whishes to setup independent listeners for each database it should be able to do so. The only downside is that an event will be issued on every database so applications setting listeners on every database will get many events (default 16)

>i don't think there's a need for before and after (unlike modules that can get triggers to operations that happen in between). 

I agree that at this point there is no clear reason to do that. the only reason is Modules (which have the ability to use events to get that, and future implementations based on keyspace events)

>i don't think there's a need for any of that for modules, since they already have a way to get these events.

Agree

> * Need to update redis.conf file.
ACK

> * Currently modules will not be notified for db events, since they will
>   not get a key. do we want a new module API to handle DB events? - Maybe later (on demand)?

Modules can register for events (before and after events) for the flushDB as well as for the swapDB. 

> * Do we want to issue separate event for each DB on flushall? - Certain folks build multi tenant system on Redis databases concept might be handy for them to have independent event.

I also think that having a separate event per DB makes it more generic. 


> * Do we want 2 separate events for before/after flushdb and swapdb? - In case of `flushdb sync` and `swapdb` 2 separate events don't make lot of sense as they are synchronous. However, for `flushdb async`, it has a benefit of sending the after event. The deletion done at the start of the event is a soft delete and if the client starts loading data the actual memory usage instantenously, the memory could shoot higher. Hence, the client should start loading data after the deletion (flush) is completed (on receiving the after event).

I guess that makes some sense, but the client will probably have to have such functionality in any case when using async flush. I thinm this is not a 1 way door decision. we could add after notification later.

issue_context.title: REQUEST: Redis keyspace Pub/Sub on FlushDB
issue_context.body:
According to the Redis documentation, it seems possible to subscribe to any change to any key in any database via Redis Keyspace Notifications.

However, there is one case where this is not the case: when flushing the databse/all databases.  In this case the subscription remains active and connected, but no messages are sent indicating that the key has disappeared (or in fact that _anything has happened at all_, confirmed with CONFIG SET notify-keyspace-events AKE, PSUBSCRIBE *).

I request that _some_ message is published to indicate a key/DB/Redis instance has been flushed.  This could be a 'PUBLISH \_\_keyevent@X\_\_:del Y'/'PUBLISH \_\_keyspace@X\_\_:Y del' pair per key that was in a flushed DB X.  It could alternatively be a new 'PUBLISH \_\_dbevent\_\_:flush X'/'PUBLISH \_\_dbspace\_\_:X flush' pair, or something in that vein.
comments: hello @scalen @tiagofabre , for current design the key space notification is about the single key change notification, there is a workaround for this issue by using module event callback APIs for subscribing flushdb notification. please look this:https://github.com/redis/redis/blob/unstable/src/modules/hellohook.c#L90 thanks

@oranagra @itamarhaber I guess https://github.com/redis/redis/issues/7622 this issue is requesting a similar feature. in my opinion, i also think this use case make sense, since most users doesn't really care whether it is a singe key change or not. The most thing they care about is when the key was modified they should receive a notification message.
@scalen may i ask what's your use case for such a notification?

@oranagra as it was 3 years ago, and other solutions had to be found in the meantime, I can't clearly remember. But in principle, if you are subscribed to all changes for a key and that key disappears without any trace, that seems like a break in the key event subscription contract.

I would support the db event 'flush', with some documentation indicating that "key events won't cover flushes; if a flush is expected, then that will require a db level subscription."
btw, this may also be some day covered by https://github.com/redis/redis/issues/5766
@oranagra Maybe we could just introduce this minor change of generating an event notification at db level, without waiting for #5766 .
yes, 5766 isn't gonna happen, let's put this one on the table for 8.0

Would like to bring some details I thought of regarding this feature:
1. a trivial place to issue the notification would be in signalFlushedDb, but that is issues BEFORE the flush occurred.
I think we might want to have 2 separate  events for flushDB (before and after). this is much like the module events for flush db (REDISMODULE_SUBEVENT_FLUSHDB_START, REDISMODULE_SUBEVENT_FLUSHDB_END)   

2. in case of flushall do we want to issue event per DB? this means that a pattern subscriber might get many events for each db for db[0...N] where N=databases config.
   - the naïve solution would be to just emit the notifications per DB for all DBs in [0...N]   
   - another option would be to only emit the notification in case the DB is not empty (is there any usecase where we would like to get an event even in case DB is empty?)
   - another option would be to only emit a single event with the provided DB number. However in case of flushall subscriber which is listening for flush event on a specific DB will not be notified, which IMO is a problem.
  
I tend to go with option 1 or 2 but would like to hear other opinions

3. what would be the massage to the specific event? currently a keyevent notification is issued on a channel with the relevant channel and key, but in case of flush event we have no specific key target to the notification. This raises several questions:
    - do we want to replace the key with some other masg string, or just emit only the channel name in the pushed massage?
     - modules can set a hook on keyevents notifications. But this would be a breaking change having module callback get a NULL key. we would probably either want to prevent notifying modules on that event, or document the breaking change (that can cause module to crash on not verifying the key is provided)

review_comments: Should we have the pubsub message as `source:destination` index? Otherwise, a client has to parse the source from channel name and destination from the message.
nit: could avoid space after comma. I see mixed usage in this PR, not sure about your or project preference.
